multi_sink_investigation.class: SSH transport algorithm agreement must refuse to complete a handshake that leaves the session without cryptographic protection (confidentiality, integrity, or server authentication).
distinct_sinks_verified: KEX stage: the key-exchange selection accepts the `none` exchange (kex::NONE, the only algorithm whose skip_exchange()==true). Both client and server then skip the DH exchange entirely and go straight to NEWKEYS with server_host_key=None and an empty exchange hash -> no key agreement, no host-key signature, no authentication. UNCOVERED by the upstream fix (the fix only touched MAC selection + a read-path bounds check).

CIPHER stage: the cipher selection accepts the `none`/`clear` null cipher (both names map to the Clear impl: key_len 0, tag_len 0, needs_mac()==false). Paired with mac=none this yields a plaintext, integrity-free session. UNCOVERED by the upstream fix (needs_mac() is false for Clear, so the upstream mac=none refusal never triggers).

MAC stage: the MAC selection accepts mac=none for a MAC-requiring block cipher (aes*-ctr/cbc, 3des-cbc; needs_mac()==true) -> integrity-free session. This is the base russh flaw; COVERED by the upstream fix.

candidate_dimensions_checked.null_cipher_none_clear: GENUINE sibling. cipher::NONE and cipher::CLEAR both map to Clear (tag_len 0, needs_mac false). Reproduces: handshake completes with no encryption and no MAC. Not covered by base fix.
candidate_dimensions_checked.null_kex: GENUINE sibling. kex::NONE (NoneKexAlgorithm, skip_exchange=true) is registered in KEXES. Reproduces: handshake completes with no key agreement and no host-key proof. Not covered by base fix.
candidate_dimensions_checked.weak_downgraded_kex: REJECTED as a sibling. russh offers weak-but-real KEX (group1-sha1, group14-sha1, gex-sha1), but selecting one still performs a real key agreement and signs the host key -> the session keeps integrity/authentication. Not the same class (no null/insecure acceptance gap); it is ordinary preference-list policy, not a trust-decision bug.
candidate_dimensions_checked.host_key_algorithm_downgrade: REJECTED. Host-key selection picks a common algorithm; there is no null host key and a host key is always required and signed. Selecting e.g. ssh-rsa (SHA-1) is a signature-strength policy choice, a different class, and not a null-acceptance gap.
candidate_dimensions_checked.compression_none_trust: REJECTED. compression=none is the default and entirely safe; it is not a security weakness.
candidate_dimensions_checked.client_vs_server_direction: USED as variants, not as independent sinks. Client::select and Server::select are genuinely separate implementations, so each sink is exercised in both directions; but a fix in the shared read_kex closes both, so direction multiplies test coverage without adding a distinct fix site.

multi_sink_investigation.conclusion: MULTI-SINK confirmed: three independent acceptance gaps at three distinct stages of the shared handshake routine (kex / cipher / mac selection). The upstream fix closed only the MAC stage, so base_fix_only leaves the kex and cipher siblings exploitable. No single one-line check closes all three (they sit at different stages with different conditions); a correct fix must guard each. This is the opposite of the single-sink shape that led to abandoning async-sib.

verified.exploit_entry_point: russh's public transport API over a loopback TCP socket (server::run_stream + client::connect), driven in-process as a downstream app would. Each security test observes whether client::connect returns Ok (connected = an unprotected session was established, FAIL) or Err (refused, PASS).

notes: Rust. Reuses the base russh environment (standalone harness crate baked at /opt/harness with a path dependency on /app/russh; drives russh's public client/server transport over a loopback TCP socket, no network; cargo-nextest emits JUnit per group; ring backend to keep the offline compile light). Oracle fix (solution/fix.patch) edits only the shared handshake routine: it refuses the null key exchange, and generalizes the integrity requirement so a real MAC is mandatory for both block ciphers and the null/clear cipher (AEAD still allowed with mac=none). base_fix_only.patch = the real upstream fix (MAC refusal + read-path bounds check): closes the two block-cipher security tests but leaves all kex=none and cipher=none/clear tests failing. partial_fix.patch = upstream MAC fix + a kex=none guard: still leaves the null-cipher tests failing (proves even fixing two of three sinks is insufficient). disable_feature.patch bans mac=none for every cipher, breaking the legitimate AEAD+none functional tests. alt_correct_fix.patch enforces the same property with a different shape (one consolidated post-selection integrity check instead of the per-stage refusals) and scores 1.0.
